Student-Teacher Unsupervised Drift Detection (STUDD)

Source: R/dfr_studd.R
dfr_studd.Rd

Unsupervised drift detector of Cerqueira, Gomes, Bifet and Torgo (2023). A classifier (the teacher) is trained on an initial window of window_size labelled observations, and a second classifier (the student) is trained on the same observations to mimic the teacher, with the teacher's predictions as its target. After that no label is used: every new observation is predicted by both models, and the mimicking error (1 when the student disagrees with the teacher, 0 otherwise) feeds a change detector, by default the Page-Hinkley test. When the detector raises an alarm, the labels of the last window_size observations are requested to retrain the teacher, and the student is retrained on the new teacher's predictions. Since the mimicking error does not depend on the labels, it is used for virtual concept drift.

Usage

dfr_studd(
  teacher,
  student = teacher,
  detector = dfr_page_hinkley(delta = 0.001),
  window_size = 500,
  student_memory = "all",
  fit_teacher = TRUE,
  target_feat = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

teacher

A daltoolbox classification object (for example daltoolbox::cla_rf("class", levels)), whose attribute is the label column of the stream.

student

A daltoolbox classification object for the student, with the same attribute and levels. By default the same algorithm as the teacher.

detector

Univariate detector fed with the mimicking errors (a dist_based or error_based object of this package). The default is the Page-Hinkley test with delta = 0.001, as in the paper.

window_size

Number of observations of the initial training window and of the window of labels requested after every drift (W in the paper).

student_memory

Observations used to retrain the student after a drift: "all" (the default, as in the reference code) uses every observation seen since the end of the initial window; "window" only the last window_size ones, which bounds memory.

fit_teacher

If TRUE (the default), the teacher is trained by the detector on the labels of the initial window and retrained after every drift. If FALSE, the teacher must already be fitted, it is never retrained and the stream needs no label column: only the student is trained, on the teacher's predictions.

target_feat

Names of the feature columns. NULL (the default) uses every numeric column except the label column.

seed

Seed of the random number generator used when the models are trained. NULL draws it from the global generator when the detector is created; the global random state is left unchanged.

Value

dfr_studd object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, for every monitored row, the class predicted by the teacher (teacher) and by the student (student), the mimicking error (error) and the detector statistic (statistic), and whether a drift was reported (drift). The classes are given by their position in the levels of the teacher. obj$labels_used counts the labels used to train the teacher.

Details

Labels are read only for the rows used to (re)train the teacher; every other row may have a missing label. The initial window is used only for training: no drift is checked on it. The rows of a drift alarm are included in the window used to retrain the teacher, as in the reference implementation (https://github.com/vcerqueira/studd, studd_batch.py).

A model is always trained on the classes present in its training data, so that, as in scikit-learn, a class missing from a window does not stop the training. When a single class is present, the model predicts that class. Predictions are the class of highest probability (the first one in case of ties). reset_state() resets the detector and keeps the models.

References

Cerqueira, V., Gomes, H. M., Bifet, A. and Torgo, L. (2023). STUDD: a student-teacher method for unsupervised concept drift detection. Machine Learning, 112, 4351-4378. doi:10.1007/s10994-022-06188-7

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
# Two classes separated by x1 + x2 = 0; from row 1201 on, the observations
# concentrate along the class boundary, where the student imitates the
# teacher worse.
n <- 2400
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * 2), ncol = 2)
x[1201:n, 2] <- -x[1201:n, 1] + stats::rnorm(1200, 0, 0.2)
y <- ifelse(x[, 1] + x[, 2] > 0, "a", "b")
stream <- data.frame(x1 = x[, 1], x2 = x[, 2], class = y)
teacher <- cla_rf("class", c("a", "b"), ntree = 20)
detector <- dfr_studd(teacher, window_size = 400, seed = 1)
model <- fit(detector, stream)
which(model$drifter_output$drift == 1)
#> integer(0)
model$labels_used
#> [1] 400
